rows.rule: Violent Unbinding (1CP Battle Tactic): Fight phase after enemy picks targets; models of the targeted GK INFANTRY unit destroyed before fighting roll D6, 4+ they fight after the attacker, then are removed. Same mechanic as CSM Daemonic Fervour, so reusing the daemonicFervour hook (threshold 4) is exact.
rows.source: wahapedia CP Aurellios' Banishers; stratagems.json gk.s.violent-unbinding vs csm.s.daemonic-fervour

rows.fix: Optional: drop the [confirm] tag on Strike Squad Sv in docs/spec/factions/grey-knights.md section 6.

rows.rule: CP page prints OC 2 for both Brotherhood Terminator Squad and Strike Squad (both BATTLELINE). Data matches.

CP page lists Purge Soul witchfire and focused witchfire with identical 24in A1 BS3+ S6 AP-2 D3; focused adds Hazardous and Precision. weapons.json matches; shared profileGroup is correct (one profile per attack).

Sanctic Hood: while leading, models in the unit get FNP 4+ vs Psychic Attacks. Rules Commentary: [PSYCHIC] weapon attacks and wounds from Psychic-tagged abilities are Psychic Attacks. Hazardous is a self-test, not an attack. attack.ts applyOnePoint implements exactly this.
rows.source: CP datasheet; Rules Commentary 'Psychic Attacks'; src/engine/attack.ts isPsychicAbilitySource
rows.fix: none (no other faction has a Psychic-tagged mortal-wound ability yet; keep the 'Psychic.' text-prefix convention when one is added)

rows.rule: Teleport Assault sets the unit up in your NEXT Movement phase and says units off-board at battle end are destroyed. That specific timing overrides the general no-round-1 / end-of-round-3 Reserves limits (the end-of-battle clause only makes sense without a round-3 cull). Commentary on repositioned units supports it.
rows.source: CP Teleport Assault text; Rules Commentary repositioned units; movement.ts eligibleArrivals and cull

rows.rule: Set-up is mandatory with no later window, so a unit not set up never returns and counts as destroyed at battle end. Engine destroys it at once instead; only kill timing differs (null attribution either way). Fallback only fires when the 3in grid search finds no spot >9in from enemies.
rows.source: CP Teleport Assault text; movement.ts arrivalCandidates / destroyTeleportingUnit
rows.fix: none needed; optional purity fix: leave the record pending and let destroyStrandedTeleports destroy it at battle end

rows.rule: Eligibility excludes units within Engagement Range of any enemy unit. inEnemyEngagement checks every on-board enemy canonical unit via leaderService.unitsInEngagement; the Daemonic Fervour bypass is hasTeleportFervour.

Core Leader rules: once the bodyguard is destroyed the Leader is a standalone unit. teleportUnitId/teleportHalves and removeUnitToReserves treat it so and clear stale links. The residual canonicalUnitId caveat is engine-wide bookkeeping, not a GK rules deviation.
rows.fix: none for GK; engine-wide detach-on-destroy is a separate cleanup

rows.rule: If GK moved first, the opponent's round-5 turn end is battle end, so a teleported unit never returns and is destroyed. The bot declining then is correct play; RAW still lets a human pick it. AI heuristic, not a rule.
rows.source: CP Teleport Assault end-of-battle clause; src/ai/utility.ts

rows.rule: Both enhancements are for the LIBRARIAN Warlord; Aurellios is the only Librarian and always Warlord, so restriction LIBRARIAN is equivalent.
Published categories: Vindictive Strategy Battle Tactic 1CP, Violent Unbinding Battle Tactic 1CP, Daemonic Fervour Strategic Ploy 2CP. Data matches; no longer a guess.
rows.fix: Optional: record the categories in grey-knights.md section 5.

rows.rule: Champion of Titan: 6VP each time your WARLORD destroys an enemy CHARACTER model, no cap. championOfTitanModelDestroyed is called once (missionService.modelDestroyed, invoked only from attack.ts); the registry missionHook has a no-op run, so no double VP.
rows.source: CP secondary text; missions.ts:719, attack.ts:1468, code-hooks.ts missionHook

rows.rule: Your battlefield edge is the mission-map edge by your deployment zone. In all six CP missions playerBattlefieldEdge's longest-contact side equals the mission's attacker edge (x=-22, or z=-15 for Clash) and its opposite; the centroid fallback never triggers.

No Escape names 'the marker closest to' each edge; no tie rule exists. A tie does occur: Scorched Earth after site-a or site-b is razed leaves north (0,6) and south (0,-6) both 22in from that edge. Code picks lowest id ('north'); spec GRE-4.2 interp says either tied marker counts.
rows.source: CP No Escape text; src/data/missions/cp-04.json; grey-knights.ts closestMarkerToEdge
rows.fix: Adopt the spec interp: closestMarkerToEdge returns all ids within 1e-6 of the minimum; noEscapeAmount needs control of any tied id per edge. Correct the spec's 'no ties' claim. Only a GW FAQ settles it.

rows.source: CP datasheet keywords; src/engine/state.ts:355; src/client/figures/data.ts KNOWN_KIT
